uncited: *   **Input:** Low-resolution (LR) views, a pre-trained 2D ISR model, and a differentiable 3D renderer producing a high-resolution (HR) rendered image $R_{HR}$.
*   **Output:** A refined HR rendered image $R_{HR}^{blur}$ and updated 3D scene parameters (e.g., Gaussian primitives) optimized against a consistency-aware loss.
It takes an image tensor as input and outputs a residual correction tensor of the same spatial dimensions.
It takes the HR rendered image as input and outputs per-pixel blur kernels.
**Super-Resolution:** Apply the pre-trained 2D ISR model to each low-resolution view to obtain an initial super-resolved image $ISR$.
**Inconsistency Simulation:** Pass the super-resolved image $ISR$ through the Inconsistency Modeling (IM) module to simulate multi-view inconsistency artifacts.
**Blur Proposal:** To prevent the IM module from overly smoothing details during optimization, predict per-pixel blur kernels $B_k$ using the Blur Proposal (BP) module.
**Loss Computation:** Compute the loss between the blurred rendered image $R_{HR}^{blur}$ and the inconsistency-simulated super-resolved image $ISR^{IM}$.
*   **Kernel Size:** The kernel size $K$ is task-dependent.
Using SwinIR to construct mipmap independently for each image without scene-level fine-tuning; 2.
*   **Time Complexity:** The method adds the computational overhead of the IM module (two residual blocks) and the BP module (four convolutional layers) per iteration.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the parameters for the IM and BP modules, as well as the per-pixel blur kernels $B_k$ during the forward pass.
*   **When to use:** When using pre-trained 2D ISR models for 3D super-resolution and observing multi-view inconsistency artifacts.
*   **When not to use:** When training a dedicated 3D super-resolution model from scratch, or when computational resources are extremely limited and the overhead of IM/BP modules is prohibitive.
